description: Crossfades between the channels of a polyphonic input, a phasor sweeping an envelope across the channels one after another

params.text: Curves the rising ramp of each channel envelope between -100% and 100%, 0% linear, negative bending toward exponential and positive toward logarithmic
Attenuates and inverts the rise CV before it is added to the RISE knob
Curves the falling ramp of each channel envelope between -100% and 100%, 0% linear, negative bending toward exponential and positive toward logarithmic
Attenuates and inverts the fall CV before it is added to the FALL knob
Sets how many channel slots each envelope spans; 1 makes the envelopes abut, below 1 leaves silence between channels, above 1 overlaps them, and the default is 2
Attenuates and inverts the width CV before it is added to the WIDTH knob
Sets what percentage of each channel envelope is held at full level; 100% gives a square envelope and 0% something between a triangle and a saw
Attenuates and inverts the hold CV before it is added to the HOLD knob
Splits the sloped part of the envelope, as the percentage given to the rise; 0% is an instant rise with a sloped fall, 100% the reverse, 50% symmetrical
Attenuates and inverts the skew CV before it is added to the SKEW knob
Sets the frequency of the internal phasor between 0.0079842Hz and 32.703Hz, at 2.044Hz by default; the ping pong shape runs at half the displayed figure
Cycles the internal phasor through forward, backward, ping pong and off, where off freezes it and by default resets it to phase 0
Sets how many polyphonic channels take part in the fade, between 0 and 16, where 0 uses every channel present at the IN input
Picks which input channel is phase 0, between 1 and 16
Sets the maximum level of the channel and sum outputs between 0% and 100%, at 100% by default
Attenuates and inverts the level CV before it is added to the LEVEL knob
Cycles the slew applied to the PHASOR input before it is summed with the internal phasor: off, 3ms per volt, 6ms per volt or 10ms per volt, which softens pops from sudden phasor jumps

inputs.text: CV added to the RISE knob through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between -100% and 100%
CV added to the FALL knob through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between -100% and 100%
CV added to the WIDTH knob through its attenuator, scaled at 1 channel slot per 0.5V, with the sum clamped between 0.0625 and 16 slots
CV added to the HOLD knob through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between 0% and 100%
CV added to the SKEW knob through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between 0% and 100%
Drives the phasor rate at a volt per octave, down to 0.0015Hz and up to 12kHz; nothing anti-aliases the high rates
Sets the phasor direction outright, overriding the button: 0V forward, 1V backward, 2V ping pong, 3V off, rounded to the nearest
Sets the channel count outright, overriding the knob, at 0.5V per channel and rounded to the nearest half volt
Sets the start channel outright, overriding the knob, at 0.5V per channel with 0.5V meaning channel 1
Summed with the internal phasor to drive the fade; 0V is phase 0 and the phase rises with voltage until 10V wraps back to phase 0, so voltages outside that range wrap around
The polyphonic signal whose channels are crossfaded
A rising edge here resets the internal phasor to phase 0
CV added to the LEVEL knob through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between 0% and 100%

outputs.text: A 10V gate for each channel whose envelope is above zero
The crossfaded signal for each channel, one per polyphonic channel
The monophonic sum of the crossfaded channel outputs
The phasor that actually drives the fade, the internal phasor and the phasor input mixed at unity, always between 0V and 10V
The envelope of each channel, one per polyphonic channel

menu: Minimize output channels — on by default, packing the fading channels into the lowest output channels; turn it off to map input channels straight through to output channels
Reset on direction turning off — on by default, sending the internal phasor back to phase 0 when the direction is set to off; turn it off to freeze the phasor and resume later

inputs.5: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.11: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
